clue.text: Gate at the Roman cross ball

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral X, shaped like a cross, stands for ten
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A gate at a Roman crossroads, with somebody annoyed at a ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gate' is the sporting sense: the number of spectators at a match.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport the gate is the crowd count paying to watch, the number present at the event.

clue.text: Host of barmy sports fans?

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the word barmy, which carries them inside

explanation.surface: The Barmy Army, England's travelling cricket supporters, described as a host.
explanation.walkthrough: The Barmy Army is the famous band of English cricket fans; 'sports fans?' points at that phrase rather than giving letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A host is a great multitude, and a military force is a vast organised multitude of soldiers.

clue.text: Packing in the ruler to see the fiddling

indicators.note: the ruler is placed in the middle of the word for packing

parts.note: to tamp is to pack down firmly
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword's queen or ruler

explanation.surface: Someone packing a ruler in their bag and being accused of fiddling.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiddling and the answer both mean meddling with something improperly, interfering to alter it.

clue.text: Can turn up at hollyhead to finally get food

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means reading the word can from bottom to top

parts.note: the head, or first letter, of holly is H

indicators.note: the final letter of the word to is wanted

explanation.surface: Someone turning up at Holyhead, the Welsh port, to get something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn up' gives NAC, can read backwards; 'hollyhead' plays on Holyhead, the Welsh ferry port, meaning the first letter of holly.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortilla chip snack from Mexican cuisine, often served with cheese and salsa, is a kind of food.

clue.text: Promote one to sit and get fat

parts.note: an ad (advertisement) promotes a product
the Roman numeral I is one
to sit for a portrait is to pose

explanation.surface: Being promoted to a desk job where one sits and gets fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Adipose describes animal tissue that stores fat, so it means fatty.

clue.text: Camp by the bed of a great lake

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
Erie is one of the five Great Lakes of North America

explanation.surface: A campsite set up by a lake shore, beside a bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Camp' is not tents but a faction within a group.
explanation.definitionFit: A camp in the sense of a faction is a small exclusive circle of like-minded people.

clue.text: Lover drops round town

indicators.note: drops means the letter for round is let fall from the word for lover

parts.note: Romeo, Shakespeare's hero, stands for any lover
the letter O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A lover leaves off doing the rounds of the town.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian capital is a city, which loosely counts as a town in crosswords.

clue.text: All right a good animal like a giraffe

parts.note: OK means all right
taken as written
pi, short for pious, means good

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether an animal resembling a giraffe is all right.
explanation.definitionFit: The forest-dwelling relative of the giraffe from the Congo is that animal.

clue.text: Office of churchmen with tree crafts

parts.note: the elder is a tree
ships are sea craft

explanation.surface: Churchmen working in an office, making things from wood.
explanation.definitionFit: In Presbyterian churches an elder holds office, and the plural noun names those positions.

clue.text: He won't talk out of order

definitions.text: He won't talk out of order

parts.words: He won't talk out of order
parts.note: seems to describe someone who keeps to the rules, but means a silent monk from a religious order

explanation.definitionFit: A Cistercian monk of the strict observance traditionally keeps silence, coming from that religious order.

clue.text: Ape from central Miami to Canadian capital

indicators.note: the central letter of Miami is taken away, leaving the outer letters
a capital letter here is the first letter of the word Canadian

explanation.surface: An ape travels from downtown Miami to Ottawa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canadian capital' looks like Ottawa but is just the capital (first) letter of Canadian; Miami loses its middle A.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape someone is to copy their manner, which is to imitate them.

clue.text: Laid between or laid to rest and put down

parts.note: to inter is to bury, to lay to rest
laid means put down

explanation.surface: Something placed between others, or buried and set down.
explanation.definitionFit: Things placed between other layers are inserted among them, the meaning of this word.

clue.text: No time set to start the action?

definitions.text: No time set to start the action?

parts.words: No time set to start the action?
parts.note: reads as a complaint about no start time, but nil plus a period of time is the military moment an operation begins

explanation.definitionFit: Military planners name the scheduled instant for launching an operation in this way.

clue.text: Anterior head of a religious order

definitions.meaning: anterior means earlier or coming before
the superior of a monastery or a deputy to an abbot

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: earlier in time, and the monk who governs a monastic house.

clue.text: Consider with methodical intention

definitions.meaning: to ponder or weigh up carefully
done on purpose and with care

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to weigh carefully; as an adjective it means intentional and unhurried.

clue.text: Remove hair to point at pile created

parts.note: E is a compass point, east

indicators.note: the letters of at pile are created afresh in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Removing hair to point at a pile it has created.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' is a compass direction, not a gesture; 'created' is the anagram signal working on the two words that follow 'point'.
explanation.definitionFit: To depilate or strip hair from the body by the roots is the meaning.

clue.text: Promote alternative take over

definitions.note: the noun sense, a taking over or takeover, as of a child or policy

parts.note: an ad promotes a product
an option is an alternative

explanation.surface: Promoting an alternative plan in a corporate takeover.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking on a child, idea or policy as one's own is this act of acceptance.

clue.text: Grave words for somebody in a pipe hat

indicators.note: the letters of pipe hat are mixed together in a heap, giving a jumbled arrangement

explanation.surface: A gravestone inscription for someone in a pipe and hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a' loosely signals rearranging PIPE HAT; 'Grave' means at a grave, not serious.
explanation.definitionFit: Words inscribed on a tombstone commemorating the dead are this kind of inscription.

clue.text: He was great to beat Greece

definitions.text: He was great to beat Greece

parts.words: He was great to beat Greece
parts.note: describes the Macedonian king, called the Great, who subdued the Greek city states

explanation.definitionFit: The Macedonian king surnamed the Great conquered Greece and much of Asia.

clue.text: Pouring out to see 5

definitions.note: refers to the answer at 5 down, a clique

indicators.note: out signals the letters of pouring are put out of their order

explanation.surface: Pouring out drinks to see someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A clique and an exclusive social circle are synonyms.

clue.text: Stipulated condition is in with a anarchist agitator

indicators.note: the word is sits in the middle of the agitator

parts.note: a Provo was a member of a 1960s Dutch anarchist movement
taken as written

explanation.surface: A condition is laid down by an anarchist rabble-rouser.
explanation.definitionFit: A clause in a contract laying down a requirement is a condition attached.

clue.text: A nitwit starts and another appears here

indicators.note: the starts of the words A nitwit, their first letters, are taken

parts.note: another nitwit, i.e. a twerp

explanation.surface: Fools turn up one after another in some place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'here' is the definition: the clue describes a place where this happens, a Belgian port.
explanation.definitionFit: The Belgian port city is the place being pointed at as a location.

clue.text: A bit spartan to find the gold stereo is unfinished

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: unfinished means the final letter of stereo is dropped

explanation.surface: A gold hi-fi that isn't finished looks rather bare.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain, severe and without comforts is how a spartan lifestyle is described.

clue.text: Was last month a triumph?

parts.note: ex means former, what was
ult., ultimo, is formal shorthand for last month

explanation.surface: Asking whether last month was a success.
explanation.definitionFit: To triumph in the sense of rejoice greatly over a success is to rejoice.

clue.text: He takes the pledge

parts.note: seems to be someone swearing off drink, but describes a pawnbroker, who takes goods as pledges, nicknamed as a relative

explanation.definitionFit: In old slang a pawnbroker was called by this family name, the relative who lends money.

clue.text: Aid bison to recover from volcanic glass

indicators.note: recovering from an upset, the letters of aid bison are reassembled

explanation.surface: Helping a bison recover from being caught in a lava flow.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark natural glass formed when lava cools very fast is this rock.

clue.text: A small drink of spirits before play

parts.note: a dram is a small measure of whisky

explanation.surface: A tot of whisky before the show.
explanation.definitionFit: A play is a theatrical piece, a work for the stage.

clue.text: Popular dish of the wild west

indicators.note: wild signals the letters of west run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A favourite meal of the Wild West.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow-cooked meat and vegetable dish is a popular everyday meal.

clue.text: Hermit told to moor ship by the point

indicators.note: told means the phrase is heard spoken rather than read on the page

parts.note: to moor a ship is to anchor it, the verb with its object

explanation.surface: A recluse is told to tie up a boat at a headland.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken quickly, the phrase anchor it runs into the recluse's title; 'by the point' adds the sense of a ship moored off a headland and supplies no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious recluse living alone in a cell is a hermit.

clue.text: Inspect German car with ford model

parts.note: Audi is a German car maker
the Model T was Ford's famous car

explanation.surface: Checking over a German car alongside a Ford.
explanation.definitionFit: To audit accounts is to examine them officially.

clue.text: Vessel for sheep, right?

parts.note: a ewe is a female sheep

explanation.surface: A vessel for a sheep, is that right?
explanation.definitionFit: A large wide-mouthed water jug is a vessel.

clue.text: One may begin to carry in a barrow fatty substance

indicators.note: the barrow carries the other letters inside it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the beginning of may is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone may start carrying a load of fat in a wheelbarrow.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft fatty tissue inside bones that produces blood cells is this substance.
